# Lifecycle subscriber

A lifecycle subscriber learns when templates and instances change. Rimsky calls one of seven callbacks and expects an empty acknowledgement back.

Proto file: `lifecycle.proto`.

## The RPCs

All seven return `LifecycleAck`, an empty message. Return it to accept the event.

| RPC | When rimsky calls it |
| --- | --- |
| `OnTemplateRegistered(OnTemplateRegisteredRequest)` | A template is registered |
| `OnTemplateDeployed(OnTemplateDeployedRequest)` | A template is deployed |
| `OnTemplateUndeployed(OnTemplateUndeployedRequest)` | A template is undeployed |
| `OnTemplateDeregistered(OnTemplateDeregisteredRequest)` | A template is deregistered |
| `OnInstanceCreated(OnInstanceCreatedRequest)` | An instance is created |
| `OnInstanceTerminated(OnInstanceTerminatedRequest)` | An instance is terminated |
| `OnRunScopeTerminal(OnRunScopeTerminalRequest)` | A run scope reaches a terminal state |

`LifecycleSubscriber` declares no `Capabilities` RPC. An operator declares you under any peer block with `protocols: [lifecycle_subscriber]`.

## The requests

| Request | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `OnTemplateRegisteredRequest` | `template_hash`, `spec` (the canonical template bytes) |
| `OnTemplateDeployedRequest` | `template_hash`, `tags` |
| `OnTemplateUndeployedRequest` | `template_hash` |
| `OnTemplateDeregisteredRequest` | `template_hash` |
| `OnInstanceCreatedRequest` | `instance_id`, `template_hash`, `instance_key`, `params`, `service_bindings`, `owner_api_key_id`, `target_routing_identity` |
| `OnInstanceTerminatedRequest` | `instance_id`, `template_hash`, `terminated_at_unix_ms` |
| `OnRunScopeTerminalRequest` | `run_scope_id`, `terminal_reason`, `instance_id` |

`spec`, `params`, and `service_bindings` carry JSON bytes.

## Who gets called

Rimsky calls only the subscribers a template references. A template names its peers, and rimsky fans an event out to that set, not to every subscriber in the deployment.

## Delivery and idempotency

Rimsky keeps a delivery ledger keyed by peer, scope kind, and scope id. Before it calls you, it reads that ledger; when the recorded state already matches the event, it skips the call. After you acknowledge, it records the new state in the same transaction.

Two consequences for your implementation:

- **Be idempotent.** Rimsky redelivers an event whose acknowledgement it failed to record.
- **Your refusal blocks the operation.** An error from your callback fails the control-API request that triggered it. A failed `OnTemplateRegistered` answers the register call with `500` and a `details` map naming each peer and its error, and the template does not register.

Answer promptly and acknowledge before doing slow work.

## The HTTP+JSON bridge

`serverkit.MountLifecycle` mounts the seven callbacks on a `http.ServeMux` as `POST /v1/on_template_registered`, `/v1/on_template_deployed`, `/v1/on_template_undeployed`, `/v1/on_template_deregistered`, `/v1/on_instance_created`, `/v1/on_instance_terminated`, and `/v1/on_run_scope_terminal`. Each takes the callback's protobuf-JSON request and returns its protobuf-JSON response.

Rimsky dials lifecycle subscribers over gRPC only. Serve gRPC and use the bridge for your own tooling.

## Observability

There is no lifecycle-subscriber observability protocol, and rimsky's observability read routes carry no lifecycle-subscriber entry. Give your subscriber its own logs and metrics.

## Proving it

```
rimsky conformance lifecycle-subscriber --endpoint grpc://localhost:9097
```

The check dials your endpoint and calls six of the seven callbacks with synthetic ids, in order: `OnTemplateRegistered`, `OnTemplateDeployed`, `OnTemplateUndeployed`, `OnTemplateDeregistered`, `OnInstanceCreated`, `OnInstanceTerminated`. It stops at the first error and names the failing callback. `OnRunScopeTerminal` is not covered; exercise it yourself.

`--tls required` dials with verified TLS against the system roots. `--transport` accepts `grpc` alone.
